verdict.rationale: Langfuse's evaluation docs list an Annotation Queues feature for manually reviewing and rating traces, and say human annotations can be combined with other evaluation methods. So the core capability is first-party. However, the evidence is only a one-line table entry repeated across pages, with no detail on how outputs are routed into queues or how labeling works. Missing for 10: documentation of how traces or outputs are routed into queues (manual or rule-based), queue assignment and reviewer workflow, label and score configuration for annotators, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can route outputs to human annotation queues for review and labeling

citations.quote: Review and rate traces manually | Annotation Queues, Scores via UI
You can combine a variety of different evaluation metrics like model-based evaluations (LLM-as-a-Judge), human annotations or fully custom evaluation workflows via API/SDKs.
